releases.summary: Persistent mode: press Space while labels are up and they stay up, so one press of the hotkey carries a run of clicks. The panel is now three tabs.
bullets: Persistent mode: with labels up, press Space. The labels stay after each click and update to match what the click changed; what did not change keeps its letters. Space again switches it off, and Esc puts the labels away. The menu bar icon is shown filled while it is on.
Tab: in persistent mode, Tab updates the labels after a change you made with the mouse or trackpad, such as a scroll. A shortcut such as ⌘T updates them by itself.

What ends it: a click into a text field, a right-click, or a button that opens a menu ends persistent mode, so your typing and the arrow keys go where you expect. So does a password field taking the keys.

Panel: three tabs, Appearance, Shortcuts and General, in place of one long screen. The switch, the hint and the label preview stay at the top. On Shortcuts, each kind of click has one menu for its key.
Colours: one palette of thirty colours for the label and for its letters. Choose Label or Letters, then a colour. The colours you had carry over.
Fixed: typing the label of a button in Jumpr's own panel no longer quits Jumpr.
Scroll mode: the menu bar icon is shown filled while scroll mode is on. On macOS 27 it had stopped showing.
releases.note: Holding a letter key no longer repeats it into labels, so a label such as AA needs two taps. A menu opened from a button gets no labels of its own; in persistent mode the press ends the mode, so the arrow keys work in it. In a web page that includes a button whose menu is drawn in the page. The log on your Mac now also records each update of the labels (app, counts and time) and why persistent mode ended, nothing more.

releases.summary: Right-click, ⌘-click, double-click and ⇧-click from a label: hold a key on the label's last letter.
bullets: More kinds of click: hold ⇧ on the last letter of a label for a right-click, ⌘ for a ⌘-click (a link opens in a new tab), ⌥ for a double-click, or ⌃ for a ⇧-click, which selects from the selected row to this one. With nothing held it clicks as before.
Your keys: the panel has a row for each of those clicks. Give it another key, or None to switch it off. Choosing a key another click has swaps the two.
Messages: every emoji showing in the emoji picker has a label. Before, only two rows did.
Scroll mode: an area inside another that has nothing to scroll no longer gets a letter. In Messages' emoji picker the whole picker is outlined, not one section of it.
releases.note: While labels are up, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ with the letter that completes a label now clicks instead of running that shortcut, unless that key's click is set to None. The menu a right-click opens gets no labels of its own; use the arrow keys in it. The log on your Mac now also records the kind of each click, nothing more.

releases.summary: Scroll mode: scroll any area on any display from the keyboard, with your pointer left where it is.
bullets: Scroll mode: press ⌘⇧J and every area that scrolls gets a letter. J and K scroll the outlined area a line, D and U half a page, G and ⇧G to the ends; hold a key to keep going. Type a letter to pick another area, F to bring the letters back, Esc or ⌘⇧J to leave.
Where it starts: the area you scrolled last in that window is already outlined, or the one with keyboard focus, so J works at once.
Shortcut: the scroll shortcut has its own row in the panel, under the label shortcut.
Mail, Messages, Claude, Discord, Slack: one letter per pane. A message in a conversation, or an email's header, is not offered as something to scroll on its own.
releases.note: Scroll mode scrolls up and down only. An area that cannot scroll may still get a letter; picking it does nothing. The log on your Mac now also records each scroll's amount and the app it went to, nothing more.

bullets: Notifications: with Notification Center open, each notification has a label. Type it to open that notification, or to expand a stack.
Update window: the update window now shows what changed.
releases.note: While Notification Center is open, windows behind it on that display get no labels, because a click outside it only closes it. The menu bar, the Dock and your other displays keep theirs.

releases.summary: A new panel in the menu bar, and Jumpr can now click itself.
bullets: One panel for everything. Click the J in the menu bar: an on/off switch, a live preview of your labels, label color, letter color, label size, the shortcut, start at login and the update check are all there. The separate Settings window is gone.
Pick colors in place. Choose from swatches or type an exact color. The system color picker is no longer used.
Letters in any color. Letters can be any color you like, or Auto, which picks black or white, whichever reads better on your label color. If you had set a letter color, it is kept.
Jumpr labels itself. Its own menu bar icon gets a label. Type it to open the panel, and every control in the panel gets a label too.
Dia: the folders in the sidebar have labels. Type one to open or close that folder.
Web pages: text a page lets you move to with the keyboard now gets a label, such as the days in a date picker. Days a page marks as unavailable are skipped.
releases.note: Not fixed, because Dia does not tell macOS they are there: the pinned tiles at the top of Dia's sidebar, and the individual spaces in the strip at its bottom (the strip gets one label).

releases.summary: Messages now gets labels on its sidebar.
bullets: Messages: every conversation in the list and every pin has a label. Type it to open that conversation.

Other apps built the same way: text that an app says can be pressed now gets a label, wherever it is. Some of it does nothing when pressed: in Messages, the time stamps between messages get labels too.

releases.summary: A housekeeping release. Nothing you see or do changes.
bullets: The license notice for Sparkle, the updater Jumpr includes, now ships inside the app.
Two debugging hooks are switched off unless Jumpr is started with a debug flag.
Code the app never used is gone.

releases.summary: The menu bar icon is now the J from Jumpr's logo, on its own with no box. It follows your menu bar: white on a dark bar, black on a light one. Nothing else changes.
The menu bar icon is now Jumpr's own yellow J label, matching the app icon and the site. Nothing else changes.
First public release. Press ⌘⇧Space and every clickable thing on every display gets a short label, usually two letters. Type the letters and it clicks.
bullets: Windows, menus, the Dock and menu bar icons
Works in Safari, Chrome and web-based apps
Checks for updates once a day; you can turn that off
Free and open source (MIT). macOS 15 or later. Built for Apple silicon and Intel; the Intel build has not yet been tested on an Intel Mac.
